name: MMT-ADR-0024 claims the scope chip supersedes nav-contract shape; code says otherwise — S6 T10's conditional deletion of navigation-contract.ts would fire on a false premise
description: DRIFT: MMT-ADR-0024 states the V2 scope chip 'supersedes mode/proxy tab-shape navigation'. Current code contradicts this — apps/mobile/src/hooks/use-navigation-contract.ts:22 hardcodes V2_TABS={mentor,subjects,journal} and :78-92 still calls resolveNavigationContract() with appContext/isParentProxy/role EVEN UNDER V2. The chip owns scope SELECTION only; it has not superseded the navigation contract. CONSEQUENCE (why this is P1 and why it was captured out-of-band): S6 T10 carries a CONDITIONAL DELETION — 'delete navigation-contract.ts if the V2 chip fully owns shape' — which reads as SATISFIED on ADR-0024's authority when it is not. If S6 T10 fires on this ADR, it deletes live navigation code on a false premise: an irreversible action justified by a document that does not match reality. SCOPE LIMIT (verified, shrinks blast radius): the authorization-wall half is governed by MMT-ADR-0027 (Accepted), NOT by ADR-0024, so no S5/S6 AUTHORIZATION step depends on 0024 — the exposure is navigation-shape only. PROVENANCE: surfaced by the WI-2062 audit (ADR-0024 disposition) on 2026-07-30. Captured separately and deliberately: WI-2062 is blocked by the Cosmo Kind guard and may stay blocked, and a finding that guards against an irreversible action must not be gated on the item that found it.
acceptanceCriteria: Retyped Bug→Documentation at triage (WI-1314 precedent: the defect is doctrine/plan prose — no runtime behavior changes; the code is RIGHT, the documents are wrong). Drift verified in code: use-navigation-contract.ts:22 hardcodes V2_TABS={mentor,subjects,journal} and ~:78-92 still calls resolveNavigationContract() with appContext/isParentProxy/role even under V2 — the scope chip owns scope SELECTION only, contradicting MMT-ADR-0024's claim that it 'supersedes mode/proxy tab-shape navigation'. The live hazard: S6 T10's conditional deletion (docs/plans/v2-plan/2026-06-10-s6-cutover-deletions.md — 'delete navigation-contract.ts if the V2 chip fully owns shape') reads as satisfied on ADR-0024's authority when it is not; firing it would delete live navigation code irreversibly. AC: (1) MMT-ADR-0024 is corrected — its supersession claim amended or the ADR re-statused so it accurately states the chip owns selection while resolveNavigationContract() still owns shape, with the code citations embedded; (2) the S6 T10 condition is rewritten to be CODE-VERIFIED, never ADR-derived: deletion may proceed only on demonstrated evidence (V2 path no longer invokes resolveNavigationContract; shape fully chip-owned; the doc names the concrete checks), and the plan doc's cross-reference to ADR-0024 reflects the corrected status; (3) the scope limit is preserved in both docs: the authorization wall is MMT-ADR-0027's (Accepted) — no S5/S6 authorization step depends on 0024; (4) coordinate with WI-2062 (ADR-0024 disposition audit, currently Kind-guard-blocked) — cite it, don't absorb it; this item's guard must land even if 2062 stays blocked. Done: no plan step can delete navigation-contract.ts on the strength of a document that contradicts the code.
riskImpact: HIGH / irreversible. An unguarded S6 T10 would delete live navigation code (navigation-contract.ts) on the strength of an ADR claim that current code contradicts. Deletion of shipped navigation logic is not cheaply reversible and would regress the standing V0 non-regression boundary. Likelihood is real rather than theoretical: the conditional is already written into S6 T10 and reads as satisfied against ADR-0024's headline. Mitigation is cheap (evaluate the condition against code, not the ADR); the cost of missing it is a production navigation regression discovered post-deletion.
